restrictions: Messages are exactly 135 bytes; each is one padded block M || 0x86 with zero capacity (520 fixed state bits). Complete fixed-zero-IV SHA3-256 sponge with suffix 0x06 and pad10*1, prefix rounds 0..4, 256-bit digest.

This package (v17) is rubenmarcus's v15 (91f1424d) with two changes, neither chosen from any run: (1) a counted T3 match step match_step (137 primitives on every path, branch-free, checked on every review against the plain active-row test on 901 real matches of the output core at three block counts, r5-count trial 10), at which P's matches and the disclosed match counts of v15's development D15 are priced (proof 2.1, 0.1); (2) S2CAP = 2^20 by the rule 'the largest power of two whose stage-2 term does not exceed E's stage-1 term', which reads no run (proof 2.6). B_BUDGET = 2^32, X_MAX = 2^23, A_MAX = 2^13, CCAP, K = 96, M_CAP and every other program, study and certificate are v15's.

v15, which v17 modifies, is winglock's v14 (f1cedf6b, co-author Th0rgal) with two phases replaced by programs that compute the same outputs: T3 of the trail search P by meet-in-the-middle on zero blocks of alpha2 with a pigeonhole certification (proof 2.1; the zero-block half-sum match is Subflatus3's, 9bccf245, used there as a check), and E's stage 1 by the counted degree-4 fast exhaustive search of Bouillaguet et al. (CHES 2010), the function v14's evidence enumerator fes.c computed (proof 2.4). B', S, the connector, the driver, K = 96 and the caps X_MAX, S2CAP, B_BUDGET and CCAP are v14's, unchanged.

No advice: the algorithm runs every phase itself, and its time is the sum of caps, fixed counts and organizer-recomputed counts times counted prices or stated bounds (proof 2, 6): P 2^30.03 units (T1, T2 as in v14; T3: 48,592,224 half vectors, 7 levels, 127 blocks, matches capped at M_CAP = 2^24, each at 137 counted + 2^11 primitives; half tables built at each level); B' 2^32 units plus one update; at most 2^13 connector attempts of at most X_MAX = 2^23 work units; E: K = 96 spaces, setup at most 2^16 units, 2^24 Gray steps of 364 counted primitives per 256 pairs, at most S2CAP = 2^20 stage-2 pairs per space. Algorithm 2^33.3814.

Development is charged as preprocessing by v14's rule (proof 0.1, H2): every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number the algorithm reads, at the counted prices of the submitted programs. v14's G2 (2^31.8877) and C (2^33.2426), with their spaces at v15's E, and v15's D15 (the abandoned contiguous-block T3 run charged as if completed, the layout comparison, the certified P run, checks; 2^34.6617 at v15's 2^9 match price, 2^33.0950 with its 7.505 x 10^10 disclosed matches, rounded down, at the counted match_step's 137 primitives). v17 made no development run. Total 2^35.0059, claimed 35.01; preprocessing 34.75. At v14's prices for G2 and C the total is 36.88; with D15 unrepriced it is 35.62: the claim rests on pricing development at the submitted programs' counted prices, as v14's rule says.

Premise P (inside H1; success only): P outputs the trail of proof 3 within M_CAP. P's native run certified it at its level of 64 blocks (W* = 127 <= 2 x 64 - 1, Lemma P: every leaf with AS(alpha2) <= 63 is found, every other leaf has w1 >= 128), with 7,251,935 matches; the organizer recomputes the structural counts, the output core's level (r5-count trial 10), seed-picked cores (r5-mitm-0, 1) and P's driver on a sub-problem with its cap. If P certified nothing it would output nothing; every cost bound holds either way.

Probability space: the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), fixed target, no advice. Success is measured end to end (proof 5): R6, v15's pre-registration (plan and code hashed before any run, 48 complete runs of v15, all reported): 44 of 48 succeed, one-sided Clopper-Pearson bound 0.8193 at 95% and 0.7768 at the organizer's alpha = 0.01. R5, v14's pre-registration: 46 of 48, bounds 0.874 and 0.8362. Both studies consist of complete runs of v17 (Lemma 6c: v17 differs only in S2CAP = 2^20, and no logged space had more than 315 stage-2 pairs). Claimed 0.40; each study alone supports it.

Executed evidence (not the claimed cost): R6 and R5 (proof 4.2, 4.7, Appendices D, E), with 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions as certificates; r5-R-0..7 re-derive 16 seed-picked R5 successes per review; r5-bpfull runs a whole B' from its label; r5-count checks the counted stage 1 step by step against plain evaluation and its longest path, the T2 leaf, P's driver and cap, and P's certifying level on the output core; r5-trail-0..3 recount T1, T2 and the half vectors.

Th0rgal (7deb1595, with Subflatus3 and rubenmarcus) introduced the zero-advice framing; winglock's v8, v13, v14 built the algorithm; rubenmarcus's v15 replaced T3 and E's stage 1; v17 adds the counted match step and the run-free S2CAP rule. Memory: largest phase about 2^28 bytes; declared 30. v17's trail_search builds and releases each core's half tables per level (one core held at a time; proof 7), removing v15's retention of all 467 cores' tables (about 2^33.3 bytes).

The nominal reference identifier does not assert an improvement over published work; no improvement on the method of Guo et al. is claimed beyond the byte-aligned adaptation, B', the counted programs and the accounting.

heuristics.statement: Averaged over all of the algorithm's own coins (B' candidate coins, connector coins), the probability p that v17's algorithm outputs a collision satisfies p >= 0.40. Premise R (run selection and coins): the SHA-256/SHAKE-256 coins of labels fixed before the runs act as fresh coins, and the 48 runs of each pre-registered study (R6, v15's; R5, v14's) are an unselected sample of the algorithm's runs, so that their success indicators are independent Bernoulli(p) draws. Premise P: P outputs the trail of proof Section 3 within M_CAP.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability. Each R6 run is a complete run of v15 with label-derived coins (proof Lemma 6a: v14's B', connector and driver code, P's certified trail, E as fes with stage 2 and S2CAP; no cap that should not act acted), and each R5 run is one too (Lemma 6b: v15 computes v14's outputs), and both are complete runs of v17 (Lemma 6c: v17 changes only S2CAP to 2^20, above every logged stage-2 count; match_step changes no decision of P). Premise P concerns success only: every cost term of P is a fixed count, an organizer-recomputed count or a cap. Output correctness and every cost cap hold without H1.
heuristics.extrapolation: R6: 44 of 48 runs succeed; under premise R the one-sided 95% Clopper-Pearson bound is 0.8193, so by R6's pre-registered rule the claim 0.40 is supported; at the organizer's alpha = 0.01 the bound is 0.7768. R5: 46 of 48, bounds 0.8746 (95%) and 0.8362 (99%). The studies are not pooled. Premise R: R6's plan, driver, analysis, launcher, enumerator and P program were hashed at 2026-10-08T00:19:33Z before any run and made read-only; every run is reported (proof 4.7, Appendix E: per-run ledger with result-file hashes); the plan's only outcome-dependent rule is whether to claim; every other run made for v15 is listed (proof 4.1). Premise P: P's native run certifies the trail by Lemma P; it agrees with v14's exhaustive T3 passes; the organizer re-runs the output core's certifying level, seed-picked cores and P's driver on a sub-problem. Organizer checks of R5 as in v14 (r5-R-0..7, r5-bpfull); 7 R6 and 8 R5 collisions are certificates.
heuristics.limitations: Label-seeded SHAKE-256 coins stand in for fresh words (premise R). R6's failures, run order and timing are logged by us; the organizer re-derives no R6 run (the experiment file's 64-KiB budget holds only R5's table), but 7 R6 collisions are certificates. R5's limitations are v14's. P's full-scale certification rests on our native run (296 CPU-s, reproducible from Appendix A); the organizer checks 3 of 467 cores per review at the certifying level.

heuristics.statement: The charged development - v14's G2 (2^31.8877 units) and C (2^33.2426 units), priced at the counted prices of the submitted programs, and v15's D15 (2^33.0950 units: v15's 2^34.6617 with its disclosed 7.505 x 10^10 matches, rounded down, repriced from 2^9 to the counted match_step's 137 primitives) - contains every target-specific run whose result fixed, or under its plan could have changed, a number that v17's algorithm reads, and these prices are the ones the cost model requires. v17 made no development run: match_step is program text, MATCH_STEP is a count of its path, and S2CAP comes from a rule that reads no run. Every other run either produced program text or fixed no number of v17.
heuristics.scope: Only the development (preprocessing) part of the time and preprocessing claims. The algorithm's own terms (2^33.3814) are caps, fixed counts and recomputed counts at counted prices or stated bounds, and do not depend on H2.
heuristics.extrapolation: Proof 0.1 lists every run with what it fixed and the claim it would give if charged (A1 40.96, A2 38.35, R5 35.74, R6 36.03, C' 41.23, D at most 36.65, A3/A4 37.06, v14's native T3 runs 36.13). Proof 0.2 gives the origin of every number of v17: analysis, counting (E_STEP, T2_LEAF, MATCH_STEP), a charged run (D15), or v17's run-free S2CAP rule. G2 and C are priced at v15's E by v14's own rule (the search, if added to the submitted program, runs on its counted routines); C's spaces were computed by fes.c, which is v15's stage 1. D15's matches are priced by the same rule at match_step, which computes the active-row test every such match performs; only the three disclosed match counts are repriced, each rounded down, and every other item keeps v15's charge. D15 charges v15's abandoned contiguous-block T3 run as if its last level had completed.
heuristics.limitations: At v14's prices for G2 and C the total is 36.88, and with D15's matches at v15's 2^9 bound it is 35.62: the improvement depends on accepting v14's pricing rule for development as applied to the submitted counted programs. A1 (v7's design study that produced B''s code) stays uncharged as in v14; charging it gives 40.96. D15's largest item is an upper bound (the stopped run is charged complete). D15's itemisation is v15's; v17 changes only the price of its disclosed matches.
